Article Title: Saransh Jain makes India debut at 33: Who is the Madhya Pradesh allrounder taking on Sri Lanka?
Article Text:
Saransh Jain (BCCI Photo)

2nd Test - Playing XIs

India XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill(c), Rishabh Pant(w), Ravindra Jadeja, Dhruv Jurel, Saransh Jain, Manav Suthar, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna

Sri Lanka XI: Lahiru Udara, Kamil Mishara, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva(c), Sonal Dinusha, Niroshan Dickwella(w), Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando

Who is Saransh Jain?

Late bloomer earns India call-up

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Saransh Jain's long wait for India recognition ended on Sunday when the 33-year-old allrounder made his Test debut against Sri Lanka in the second match of the series.Jain was presented his India cap by veteran allrounder Ravindra Jadeja during the team's huddle, marking the culmination of a domestic career that has stretched over a decade.His debut also makes Jain the first India player to make his international debut after turning 33 since Robin Singh in 1998.India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and opted to bat first, backing his team to make the most of the conditions."Batting first, yes. It looks like a much harder wicket than Galle. The pitch got slower and started to turn, but this will be a good wicket to bat on," Gill said.Born in Madhya Pradesh, Jain is a left-handed batter and right-arm offspinner whose strongest credentials have come in red-ball cricket.In 54 first-class matches, he has scored 2,223 runs at an average of 31.75 and taken 188 wickets at 27.30. He has also played 67 List A and 20 T20 matches, but it was his consistency in the longer format that eventually pushed him into India's reckoning.Jain is the son of former first-class cricketer Subodh Jain and has spent much of his career away from the spotlight.He made his Ranji Trophy debut in 2014 but emerged as a significant domestic performer only in 2022.Having played just eight first-class matches until then, Jain starred in the Ranji Trophy knockouts for Madhya Pradesh, taking 13 wickets and scoring a half-century as the team won its maiden title.The latest Ranji Trophy season was arguably Jain's best yet. He scored 518 runs at an impressive average of 57.55 and claimed 30 wickets at 20.43.That came after an outstanding Duleep Trophy campaign for Central Zone, where Jain scored two half-centuries and took 16 wickets across two matches to earn Player of the Series honours.His performances eventually brought him closer to the India setup. Last month, Jain was among the net bowlers preparing India's batters ahead of the one-off Test against Afghanistan in New Chandigarh.Now, after years of domestic cricket and a breakthrough in his early 30s, Jain has finally received his opportunity at the highest level — making his India debut at an age when most players are already well into their international careers.
Article Summary: Saransh Jain made his Test debut for India against Sri Lanka on Sunday. The 33-year-old allrounder is the first India player to make his international debut after turning 33 since Robin Singh in 1998. Jain was presented his India cap by veteran allrounder Ravindra Jadeja during the team's huddle.

Article Title: Portugal get their revenge on Spain — this time in cricket — after FIFA World Cup heartbreak
Article Text:
Portugal team after the win against Spain. (Pic credit: ICC)

Portugal turn the tables on Spain

Portugal close the door on Spain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Portugal have found a rather unexpected way to avenge their FIFA World Cup heartbreak against Spain.Just over a month after Cristiano Ronaldo and Co. were knocked out of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by their neighbours, Portugal got one back — not on a football pitch, but on a cricket field.Portugal defeated Spain by 57 runs in the final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Sub Regional Qualifier C in 2026, ending Spain's campaign and keeping their own dream of reaching the 2028 T20 World Cup alive.The football defeat had come in July, when Spain edged Portugal 1-0 in the Round of 16 at the Dallas Stadium in Arlington, USA. Mikel Merino scored the decisive goal in stoppage time of regulation time, sending Ronaldo's Portugal out of the tournament.This time, though, it was Portugal celebrating at Spain's expense.Led by former Australia international Moises Henriques , Portugal produced a composed performance to claim the crucial qualifying victory.Spain captain Christian Munoz-Mills won the toss and chose to field, but Portugal built a competitive total of 160/6.Dhavalkumar Norotam made 23 and Christopher De Freitas scored 39 as Portugal made a steady start without quite managing to dominate the Spanish attack.Henriques, meanwhile, contributed 18 but could not convert his start into a substantial innings.Portugal accelerated late in the innings through Craig Cachopa, who struck 25 off 21 balls, while Carlos Nunes added 15 off nine. Jeremy Martins provided an important final push with an unbeaten 18 off just eight deliveries.Yasir Ali and Lorne Burns were Spain's best bowlers, taking two wickets apiece.Spain's chase initially threatened to become interesting, but Portugal's bowlers quickly put the brakes on the pursuit.Sebastian de Oliveira made the breakthrough early, while Martins also chipped in as Portugal reduced Spain to 32/3. Yasir Ali and Daniel Doyle Calle then began rebuilding the innings and gave Spain hope of mounting a serious chase.Siraj Ullah Khadem changed the complexion of the contest in the 11th over when he bowled Yasir for 29.With the pitch making life difficult for incoming batters, Portugal steadily tightened their grip. Khadem finished with impressive figures of 2/19, while Edward Fleming delivered the decisive blow with a three-wicket haul for just 13 runs.Spain's promising chase soon turned into a procession, and Martins completed the job by bowling Lorne Burns as Portugal wrapped up a 57-run victory.The triumph sends Portugal into the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Qualifier in 2027, putting them one step closer to a place in the global qualifying tournament for the 2028 T20 World Cup.Portugal join Jersey and Denmark in the Europe Qualifier, while Scotland enter directly because of the exceptional circumstances surrounding their participation in the 2026 T20 World Cup. Italy and the Netherlands, meanwhile, advance directly to the Global Qualifier.For Portugal, the result offers a wonderfully light-hearted twist to their recent sporting rivalry with Spain: Spain may have won the football battle, but Portugal have claimed the cricket rematch.
Article Summary: Portugal defeated Spain by 57 runs in the final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Sub Regional Qualifier C in 2026. The result comes just over a month after Portugal were knocked out of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by their neighbours.

Article Title: Shoriful Islam makes Bangladesh history with record seven-wicket haul against Australia
Article Text:
Shoriful Islam

Shoriful tears through Australia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Starc strikes again as Bangladesh struggle

Bangladesh pacer Shoriful Islam etched his name in the record books on the second day of the second Test against Australia in Mackay, becoming the first bowler from his country to claim a seven-wicket haul against Australia. He also became the first Bangladesh bowler to take seven wickets in a Test innings, with his sensational figures of 7/48 now the best-ever by a Bangladesh pacer in Tests.Shoriful produced a sensational spell of 7/48 in 15 overs to overshadow Mitchell Starc 's six-wicket haul and keep Bangladesh alive in a Test that appeared to be slipping away after they were bowled out for just 64.The left-arm pacer also registered the best figures by a Bangladesh bowler away from home in Tests, surpassing Taijul Islam's 7/138 against Zimbabwe in Harare earlier this year.Australia began their innings at 41/3 but recovered through a 77-run partnership between Steve Smith and Cameron Green. Smith made 42 off 74 balls, including six fours, while Green continued the repair work with a fluent 67 off 105 balls, hitting 10 boundaries.Shoriful, however, kept Bangladesh in the contest with his pace, movement and bounce. He eventually reduced Australia to 148/8 before the hosts' lower order mounted another resistance.Green and Nathan Lyon added 38 runs before Shoriful ended Green's resistance with a pinpoint yorker to complete his magnificent seven-wicket haul. Lyon then remained unbeaten on 32 off 62 balls, including four boundaries and a six, and helped Australia reach 210.Lyon and Josh Hazlewood added another 24 runs for the final wicket, frustrating Bangladesh before Taijul Islam dismissed Hazlewood to end the innings.Australia's total gave them a commanding 146-run first-innings lead.Shoriful's achievement came only one Test after Hasan Mahmud had set a new Bangladesh record against Australia with 6/55 in Darwin. Hasan's nine wickets in that match helped Bangladesh secure their first-ever Test victory in Australia.Earlier, Australia had won the toss and opted to field, with Starc responding to Bangladesh's first-Test victory in emphatic fashion.The left-arm quick tore through the Bangladesh batting lineup with astonishing figures of 6/12, while Pat Cummins claimed three wickets as the visitors were dismissed for just 64. Shoriful was Bangladesh's top scorer with 14.Bangladesh began their second innings under pressure and reached 39/3 by the end of the first session. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto was unbeaten on 23, with Mushfiqur Rahim on four.Starc had already taken two wickets, while Cummins added one as Bangladesh trailed by 107 runs.Despite Shoriful's historic spell, Australia remain firmly in control and Bangladesh face a daunting task to avoid conceding the series-levelling Test.
Article Summary: Shoriful Islam becomes the first bowler from his country to claim a seven-wicket haul against Australia. He also became the first Bangladesh bowler to take seven wickets in a Test innings, with his sensational figures of 7/48 now the best- ever by a Bangladesh pacer in Tests. Mitchell Starc took six wickets for Australia, while Pat Cummins took three.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo becomes first player in the Football history to achieve unprecedented feat
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo (Agency Image)

Ronaldo extends historic scoring streak

977 career goals and counting

Team/Club Goals Real Madrid 450 Portugal 146 Manchester United 145 Al-Nassr 130 Juventus 101 Sporting CP 5 Total 977

Ronaldo's race to 1,000 goals

Cristiano Ronaldo has added another remarkable milestone to his extraordinary career, becoming the first professional footballer to score in 25 consecutive league seasons. The 41-year-old Portuguese superstar achieved the feat on Friday, August 21, during Al-Nassr's Saudi Pro League clash against Al-Riyadh.Ronaldo began his senior scoring run during the 2002-03 season, when he found the net for Sporting CP as a teenager. More than two decades later, that streak remains unbroken. His latest goal came after he was introduced as a substitute in the 62nd minute. Ronaldo eventually found the net in the 83rd minute, converting a low cross from Ayman Yahya with a composed left-footed finish from inside the area.The goal saw Ronaldo surpass Swedish great Zlatan Ibrahimović, who had previously held the record with goals in 24 consecutive league seasons.The landmark strike took Ronaldo's official senior career tally to 977 goals for club and country. His goals have come across five clubs and the Portugal national team:Ronaldo's latest effort also helped Al-Nassr secure a 4-0 away victory over Al-Riyadh, giving the defending Saudi Pro League champions a perfect start to their 2026-27 campaign.The historic achievement comes as Ronaldo continues his pursuit of the extraordinary 1,000-goal milestone. The Portuguese forward is now just 23 goals short of reaching four figures in official senior football.However, the next chapter of his career could also be his final one. Ronaldo recently indicated that the 2026-27 season could probably be his last in professional football, while his current Al-Nassr contract runs until June 2027.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has become the first professional footballer to score in 25 consecutive league seasons. The 41-year-old Portuguese superstar achieved the feat on Friday, August 21, during Al-Nassr's Saudi Pro League clash against Al- Riyadh. The landmark strike took Ronaldo's official senior career tally to 977 goals for club and country.

Article Title: Jamal Musiala to miss Bayern’s Supercup opener as club reveals shocking cause behind recent collapses
Article Text:
Jamal Musiala collapses again during Bayern match, reveals diagnosis and reassures fans he remains optimistic/ Image: X

Musiala ruled out of Bayern's first trophy match

The Athletic

Medication change linked to the two episodes

What happened to Musiala?

Jamal Musiala collapsed mid-game shortly after scoring, with extreme heat reportedly linked to dizziness and circulatory problems/ Image:X

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bayern take no chances with their key player

Bayern Munich will be without Jamal Musiala for Saturday’s German Supercup against Borussia Dortmund, with the club choosing not to rush the midfielder back after he collapsed during two successive pre-season matches.The decision comes after Musiala revealed earlier this week that he had been diagnosed with “temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures” caused by a neurological dysfunction. Bayern have since explained that the episodes became visible following a change in his medication, and the club is now adjusting his treatment.According to, Bayern have confirmed that Musiala will not be included in the squad for Saturday’s Supercup.Head coach Vincent Kompany said the 23-year-old has been training individually this week as the club works with medical experts and adjusts his treatment.“It’s the first time for the public, so obviously a lot of questions arise,” Kompany said. “We’ve been dealing with it for longer, though. That initial shock was a while ago, since then we’ve been given a lot more information and have made decisions with the help of the best experts.”Kompany added that Musiala has the full support of the club and that Bayern are optimistic about his situation.“Jamal has the support of everyone. Internally we’re at a point where we’re not speaking about it much anymore. We’ve been prepared for it for a long time, have our processes and are very optimistic,” he said.Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl explained that Musiala's two recent collapses occurred after a change to his medication.“He changed something in the medication, which is why the episodes became visible,” Eberl said. “Now we want to get back to where it was before, when these episodes didn’t occur.”“He’s made a huge step forward in his football. He’s showing it in training too. We’re looking forward to when he can show that in matches again. He’s not in the squad for tomorrow. It’s about adapting to the treatment.”Musiala collapsed during Bayern's friendly against RB Leipzig on Saturday after appearing dazed and losing his balance. He was helped safely to the ground by teammates before being attended to by the medical staff.Four days later, he suffered another episode during the friendly against Heidenheim, collapsing just minutes after coming on as a substitute. On both occasions, Bayern's medical staff immediately attended to him while players from both teams helped shield him from view.Musiala was able to leave the pitch on his own on both occasions, although he appeared disoriented.Following the Heidenheim incident, Musiala explained his diagnosis on Instagram.“I’ve been diagnosed with temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction,” he wrote.“These can lead to the recent incidents, like the one against Leipzig or now in Heidenheim.”Musiala also sought to reassure supporters about his condition, writing: “I know these things might seem scary at first glance — but for me, they’re currently part of my everyday life. I’m receiving the best medical treatment and am very optimistic. Importantly, there is no further health risk. I have a very good feeling and am on the right track.”Eberl said Musiala himself wanted to explain the situation publicly.“It was Jamal’s wish to communicate it,” Eberl said. “Internally we’ve known about it for longer, including the players. For us it’s become everyday life.”Musiala remains one of Bayern's most important players, with Transfermarkt valuing the 23-year-old at €100 million.His absence is therefore significant as Bayern prepare for their first opportunity to win silverware of the new season. The Supercup brings together last season's Bundesliga champions Bayern and runners-up Dortmund.Bayern won the Bundesliga for a second consecutive season, while Dortmund finished second.For now, however, Musiala's return to competitive action will wait. Bayern's immediate priority is getting his treatment back to the point where the recent episodes no longer occur before considering his return to matches.
Article Summary: Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala has been ruled out of Saturday's German Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. The 23-year-old suffered two collapses during pre-season matches against RB Leipzig and Heidenheim. He revealed earlier this week that he had been diagnosed with “temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures” caused by a neurological dysfunction. Bayern have explained that the episodes became visible following a change in his medication, and the club is now adjusting his treatment.

Article Title: Ancy Sojan: Thrissur girl who broke 22-year-old record, now aiming for Asiad gold
Article Text:
Kerala's Ancy Sojan (PTI Photo)

Forged in sand

Backwater bounty

Kerala vs Karnataka: Record rivalry

Kerala vs Karnataka

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Ancy Sojan was around three when Anju Bobby George launched herself into the air at the end of a brisk run-up in Athens and set a seemingly unsurpassable national long-jump record. For much of the two decades that followed, Ancy may not have spent a lot of time thinking about George’s record, because her sights were set elsewhere, on the athletics track — remarkable for someone who would eventually overhaul the mark that had stood for 22 years.Now, the girl from Thrissur in central Kerala is looking to write the next chapter in the story at next month’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. She’ll get to warm up for Japan at two events in India. The first of those comes next week in Bhubaneswar, the city where she jumped 6.88m in June to better George’s 6.83m set in 2004.Gearing up for another stab at international glory — she had won the long-jump silver at the last Asian Games — if the 25-year-old gets a moment to reflect on her journey, she would undoubtedly find herself back on the vast shoreline of Nattika, the unlikely setting that put her on the path to becoming an elite athlete.Ancy’s father, an autorickshaw driver, used to bring his daughter to the beach in Nattika, where she would sprint on the loose sands, dreaming of becoming a sprinter. But destiny had other plans.“Unknowingly, Ancy was putting herself through nature’s own strength training programme. Running on that loose sand builds strength in the calves and ankles,” said P Ramachandran, the sprinter from Nattika who competed in the 2000 Sydney Olympics 4x400m relay.Ancy’s coach, Anoop Joseph, echoes the thought.“Running on the uneven surface of the sand forces your ankles, feet and core to stabilise your body. It can help maintain control during approach and takeoff,” he explains.Ancy made the switch to long jump around 2015, when she won bronze with a 4.93m jump at the U-14 state school games. Then, in 2019, she burst onto the Indian athletics scene with a 6.26m jump at the National School Athletics meet in Sangrur, Punjab.Sanoj VV, her childhood coach who played a pivotal role in Ancy’s transition from a sprinter to a long jumper, remembers the spark he had seen then.“Back then I had predicted that Ancy would break George’s national record. People laughed at me. Today my prediction has come true,” he said, adding that “it was remarkable considering she was so tiny back then”.Following her feat in Bhubaneswar, accolades have poured in for Ancy from several quarters, including a congratulatory call from Kerala chief minister V D Satheeshan.When asked about his ward’s 6.88m leap, Anoop, however, chose to downplay it.“Technically, it was a perfect jump. But let’s not get carried away. We’re still working on her motor qualities, speed and strength,” he said.Anoop has a point. Records in women’s long jump tend to have surprising longevity. The world record, of 7.52m, was set by erstwhile USSR’s Galina Chistyakova in 1988, the same year that the US’ Jackie Joyner-Kersee set the Olympic record of 7.4m at Seoul.Ancy had won her Asian Games silver with a jump of 6.63m, much below her best. The gold in the last edition, held in China, was bagged by the host country’s Xiong Shiqi with a 6.73m jump.For Ancy, the run-up to Japan — apart from the World Athletics Continental Tour in Bhubaneswar, which begins on August 22, she’ll also take part in the Indian Athletics Series in Delhi from September 10 — comes against the backdrop of a personal worry.“My father is recovering from an injury, and his mobility remains restricted. He has not resumed driving his autorickshaw. It remains a concern,” she told TOI.A fishing hamlet known for its frequent dolphin sightings, Nattika is also part of cinema lore as the backdrop for the timeless, National Award-winning Malayalam film ‘Chemmeen’. Part of its claim to fame is also the raft of Olympians and international athletes that it has given India.Apart from Ramachandran, Nattika has produced Anjali P D, a track athlete, and discus thrower Athulya P. Volleyball also has a good following in this sports-loving village.“But no one from Nattika has managed to capture the national imagination like Ancy,” Ramachandran said.Yet, the village lacks a Sports Authority of India centre and is still waiting for a 400m synthetic track for budding athletes.“Aspiring athletes from Nattika have to travel to Kunnamkulam or the SAI centre in Palakkad, which typically takes at least two hours of travel by road,” Ramachandran said.In recent years, Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P T Usha has been campaigning for a synthetic track at the Corporation Stadium in Thrissur.“The progress has been slow,” said Sanoj VV.Sanoj had trained his ward till she was 18 at a ramshackle sand pit on the fringes of the National Fisheries Higher Secondary School in Nattika.“We created a makeshift sand pit for Ancy’s training back then,” he said. “Last year, the government inaugurated a modest 200-metre synthetic track here.”The progression of the national women’s long-jump record has been a two-way battle between Karnataka and Kerala. The elite list features no more than seven athletes who’ve held the record since Karnataka’s Angel Mary Joseph became the first Indian to breach the 6m mark in 1978.Till Ancy Sojan set the new mark of 6.88m in Bhubaneswar in June this year, the honours were evenly split between the two southern states.Mercy Mathew, who held the record in the early 1980s, says she was surprised that Anju Bobby George’s stay at the top lasted 22 years.Talking about Ancy, she feels the girl from Thrissur is capable of bigger leaps.“I wonder why it took this long (for George’s record to be broken), though there were quite a few who looked capable of breaking her mark,” she said. “Those were the days when we knew nothing about records. My first national record came at the inter-university meet in February 1980 in Pune,” she recalled.Mercy said Ancy is capable of adding another 10-12cm to the new record.“I’ve seen her progress from the days when she competed at the school games. She is an aggressive athlete and is capable of giving her best under pressure,” Mercy, who runs her own athletics academy in Kochi, told TOI.Mercy’s best of 6.26m came at the 1982 Asian Games, where she won silver.George’s era began with a record-breaking 6.37m on August 3, 1999, and she then took charge of the record book, improving her mark before producing her personal best of 6.83m in the 2004 Olympics final.
Article Summary: Ancy Sojan won the long-jump silver at the last Asian Games. She jumped 6.88m in June to better Anju Bobby George’s 6.83m set in 2004. The 25-year-old is looking to write the next chapter in the story at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games next month.

Article Title: Lakshya Sen suffers stunning upset, but Ayush Shetty and PV Sindhu march on
Article Text:
India's PV Sindhu (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: A stunned silence swept across the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium as India’s premier men’s singles hope, Lakshya Sen, cracked under the weight of expectations. In a major upset at the BWF World Championships 2026, the world No. 14 shuttler crashed out in the second round, humbled 19-21, 21-19, 21-17 by USA’s unheralded Garret Tan, ranked 92nd, in a gruelling 73-minute contest.Lakshya’s display on Wednesday was alarmingly inconsistent, plagued by baffling errors in judgement. While Tan grappled with the drift, Lakshya appeared perpetually unsettled.Much like his sluggish opening-round encounter, Lakshya started at a pedestrian pace, searching fruitlessly for timing while the American settled quickly. The Indian did manage to summon a fleeting burst of resolve midway through the opening game, rattling off late points to erase a deficit, level the score and snatch the opener 21-19.Yet, any expectations that the opening-game heist would settle Lakshya’s nerves were swiftly extinguished.The ensuing two games exposed glaring tactical vulnerabilities. Missing routine shots proved to be Lakshya’s bane. Even as he scrapped to stay within touching distance in the second game, Tan held firm in the clutch moments to edge it 21-19 and draw level.The decider laid bare Lakshya’s unravelling. A barrage of unforced errors leaked from his racquet. The contest took a dramatic turn when Tan began suffering from severe cramps midway through the third game.Writhing in pain between points, it momentarily seemed the American might be forced to retire. Yet, rather than pouncing on a physically compromised opponent, Lakshya remained hesitant and flat-footed. Showing remarkable courage, Tan soldiered through to keep his nose in front.Though Lakshya attempted a frantic late fightback, the gap was simply too wide to bridge.“I would give a lot of credit to my opponent; he played a very solid game. I think I gave it my all in the end, but it was just not enough to win this match,” Lakshya said.While Lakshya’s shock exit cast a shadow over the home crowd, the 21-year-old sensation Ayush Shetty provided an electric lift. Shetty dismantled Sri Lanka’s Duminda Abeywickrama 21-8, 21-10 in a breathless 26-minute masterclass to cruise into the pre-quarterfinals.Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu also advanced to the pre-quarters, subduing Canada’s Wen Yu Zhang 21-16, 21-17 in 35 minutes. Although Zhang staged a brief fightback to draw level in the second game, Sindhu shifted gears midway to pull away for a straight-games victory.However, there was heartbreak for 18-year-old Unnati Hooda in the women’s singles draw. The teenager pushed Canada’s experienced 13th seed Michelle Li to the absolute limit across 58 minutes before narrowly bowing out 21-11, 9-21, 21-23.India’s mixed doubles pairing of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto raced past Macau’s Leong Iok Chong and Ng Weng Chi 21-11, 21-11 in just 30 minutes to advance.The men’s doubles campaign suffered a setback as Arjun MR and Hariharan Amsakarunan lost 17-21, 14-21 to South Korea’s Kang Min Hyuk and Ki Dong Ju in 43 minutes.Satwik-Chirag duo gets walkoverIndia’s top-ranked men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty moved into the pre-quarterfinals without hitting a shot after Scotland’s Alexander Dunn and Adam Pringle withdrew from their scheduled second-round clash here on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen, India's premier men's singles hope, cracked under the weight of expectations. The world No. 14 shuttler crashed out in the second round, humbled by USA’s unheralded Garret Tan, ranked 92nd, in a gruelling 73-minute contest.

Article Title: After shocking Darwin defeat, Australia make big change for Bangladesh Test
Article Text:
Australian captain Pat Cummins, second left, leads his players from the field following their nine wicket loss to Bangladesh AP/PTI)

Australia's playing XI for the second Test is:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Australia have confirmed a key change at the top of their batting order for the second Test against Bangladesh, with recalled opener Matthew Renshaw set to make his return to the Test side in Mackay.Captain Pat Cummins confirmed in his pre-match press conference that Renshaw will open the innings after Australia made changes following their shock nine-wicket defeat in the series opener in Darwin.The second Test will mark Renshaw’s return to Test cricket after more than three years. The 30-year-old last played a Test in Delhi against India in 2023, when he appeared as a concussion substitute for regular opener David Warner.Since then, Renshaw has continued to represent Australia in ODI and T20I cricket, but his latest recall comes after Australia’s top order struggled badly in the opening Test against Bangladesh.Renshaw has replaced Jake Weatherald, who has been dropped after the defeat. Marnus Labuschagne and Beau Webster are expected to retain their places in the batting line-up.Australia also faced a major selection call over veteran spinner Nathan Lyon . Lyon managed only one wicket in the first Test, prompting discussion about whether Australia could go with an all-pace attack as they look to level the two-match series.However, Australia have ultimately decided to retain Lyon. The selectors confirmed his place in the XI shortly after Cummins addressed the media.Matthew Renshaw, Travis Head, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith, Cameron Green, Alex Carey (wk), Beau Webster, Pat Cummins (c), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.The decision to retain Lyon is significant given Australia's recent willingness to rely entirely on pace in certain conditions. The team used an all-seam attack twice in pink-ball Tests last year.However, leaving Lyon out of a red-ball Test when fit would have been a major break from tradition. The last time Australia omitted the veteran spinner from a Test despite him being fit was 14 years ago, at the WACA Ground in 2012.Australia now face a must-win Test in Mackay after Bangladesh took a 1-0 lead in the series with their nine-wicket victory in Darwin. Renshaw's return at the top and Lyon's continued presence in the attack will be central to Australia's attempt to bounce back.
Article Summary: Matthew Renshaw set to make his return to the Test side in Mackay. The 30-year- old last played a Test in Delhi against India in 2023. Australia face a must-win Test after losing the first Test by nine wickets. Marnus Labuschagne and Beau Webster are expected to retain their places.

Article Title: 'Here we go': Carlos Alcaraz confirms US Open return after four-month injury layoff
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, reacts during the men's singles final of the US Open tennis championships Jannik Sinner, of Italy, Sunday, Sept. 7, 2025, in New York. (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Carlos Alcaraz will return to competitive tennis at the US Open later this month as he begins his comeback from a right wrist injury that has kept him out since April.“Here we go,” Alcaraz wrote on his social media accounts on Thursday, along with a picture of himself in front of the US Open logo.The seven-time Grand Slam champion confirmed that he will compete at the tournament, scheduled from August 30 to September 13. His absence had included the French Open, Wimbledon and the North American hard-court tournaments in Toronto and Cincinnati.Alcaraz had initially planned to return at Cincinnati, where he was the defending champion, but decided to give his wrist more time to recover. He has gradually increased his workload in training and recently practised with Denmark's Holger Rune in Murcia while testing his wrist at greater intensity.The Spaniard has been out since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April after winning his opening match because of the injury.Before the injury, Alcaraz had made a 22-3 start to the season. He won the Australian Open after claiming his second US Open title last year, when he beat Jannik Sinner in the final.Despite missing several tournaments, Alcaraz remains No. 2 in the ATP rankings.His return was also announced in the style of a football transfer by reporter Fabrizio Romano on Instagram.Romano posted “Here we go!” while confirming that Alcaraz would return at the US Open.New York has been an important venue in Alcaraz's career. He won his first Grand Slam title at the 2022 US Open, becoming the youngest man to reach No. 1 in the ATP rankings at 19.Alcaraz will now return to the same tournament where he won his first major title and will look to defend his crown after missing more than four months of competition.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz will return to competitive tennis at the US Open later this month. The seven-time Grand Slam champion confirmed that he will compete at the tournament, scheduled from August 30 to September 13. The Spaniard has been out since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April after winning his opening match.

Article Title: Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand end India’s 15-year wait, assure World Championships medal
Article Text:
India's Gayatri Gopichand Pullela, right, and Treesa Jolly (AP Photo)

India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a World Championships medal after producing a superb comeback victory over China’s Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian in the women’s doubles quarterfinals on Friday.The unseeded Indian pair fought for 69 minutes before overcoming their Chinese opponents 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 to book their place in the last four. The victory guarantees Treesa and Gayatri at least a bronze medal at the championships.Their achievement is particularly significant for Indian women’s doubles badminton. The country’s last World Championships medal in the event came in 2011, when Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa claimed bronze in London.Backed by strong home support, Treesa and Gayatri recovered from a slow start and gradually took control of the contest. After dropping the opening game, the Indians sharpened their attacking play, finding greater success with their smashes and producing cleaner work around the net.The semifinal appearance marks another major milestone for a pair that has already enjoyed success on the international circuit.Treesa and Gayatri reached the All England Open semifinals in consecutive years in 2022 and 2023. They also won bronze at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and broke into the world’s top 10 at the beginning of last year.Their progress was interrupted earlier this year when Treesa suffered a serious ankle injury during training ahead of the Asia Badminton Championships and Uber Cup.The injury occurred when Treesa accidentally stepped on Gayatri’s foot during practice and twisted her ankle. An MRI subsequently revealed two high-grade muscle tears and two ligament tears, forcing her into a lengthy rehabilitation programme.The pair eventually began their comeback at the Indonesia Open before competing at the US Open. They then won the Philippine International Challenge earlier this month, providing further evidence that they were returning to their best.Now, that comeback has reached its biggest moment yet, with Treesa and Gayatri assured of a place on the World Championships podium.

The victory guarantees Treesa and gayatri at least a bronze medal at the championships.

Article Title: 'Crowd was amazing': Treesa-Gayatri reveal how home crowd helped them stun world no. 4 pair
Article Text:
India's Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopich defeat China's Zhang Shuxian and Jia Yifan (ANI Photo)

Gopichand's advice makes the difference

'We just want to stay calm'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Following in the footsteps of Jwala and Ashwini

Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand produced one of the biggest victories of their careers as they stunned world No. 4 Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian to storm into the semifinals of the BWF World Championships and secure India's first medal at the ongoing edition. The Indian duo overcame a slow start to script a remarkable comeback, defeating the Chinese pair 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 in a thrilling 70-minute quarter-final at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium.The victory ended India's long wait for a medal in women's doubles at the World Championships. Treesa and Gayatri became only the second Indian women's doubles pair to win a Worlds medal, following Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa , who claimed bronze in 2011.The home crowd played a crucial role in lifting the Indian pair during the tense encounter, with Treesa and Gayatri acknowledging the energy and support from the stands after their stunning victory."We're really happy that we converted this win into this semifinal and getting a medal, but it's not stopping yet. There are matches coming tomorrow also," Treesa told reporters after the win."And obviously, I want to thank, I think it's teamwork for us, everyone that helped us to achieve this, and really grateful, and obviously I want to thank the home crowd people. I think the crowd was amazing today; that was really giving positive vibes to us," she added.The Indian pair also revealed the advice they received from chief national coach and legendary former shuttler Pullela Gopichand during the tense battle. With the match slipping away after they lost the opening game, Gopichand urged the duo to remain composed and focus on the present moment."From the start, he was telling that be in the present moment and very calm, because that helped us score the points, and that really worked today," Treesa said."We were just be patient and waiting for the right time to score the points. I think that really worked," she added.Treesa and Gayatri had entered the quarter-final with a difficult record against Jia and Zhang, having lost all three of their previous meetings against the Chinese pair. They once again found themselves under pressure after dropping the opening game, but the Indians dramatically changed the momentum in the second game.Their composure under pressure eventually helped them complete a memorable comeback and book a place in the last four.The Indian duo will now face top seeds Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning of China in the semifinals. Gayatri said the pair will look to stick to the same approach that helped them overcome Jia and Zhang."It was a pretty tough match. We were down, trailing, and then even in the second set it was very tricky, but then we told each other to stay calm, and I think that's what we're going to do tomorrow as well," Gayatri said."We just want to stay calm, and we just want to get on court and give our 100 per cent, just enjoy as we did today," she added.Treesa and Gayatri also drew inspiration from Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa, the first Indian women's doubles pair to win a World Championships medal."Yeah, 100%. I think they're one of the ideals for us. They have created history for India in women's doubles, and I always praise and admire them," Treesa said.
Article Summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand beat world No. 4 Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian 16-21 21-15 21-13. Victory ends India's long wait for a medal in women's doubles at the World Championships. Indian duo will now face top seeds Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning of China in the semifinals.

Article Title: ‘Rankings do not matter, we are not struggling’: Gautam Gambhir unfazed by India’s Test run
Article Text:
India's Coach Gautam Gambhir, right, with Chief Selector Ajit Agarkar (PTI Photo)

India head coach Gautam Gambhir has called for more three-Test series, saying they give teams an opportunity to recover after losing the opening match.“Ideally, I would want a three-match Test series,” Gambhir said. “I’ve always believed there should be a possibility for a team that loses the first Test to come back and win the series. You can’t do that in a two-Test series, the most you can do is draw it. A short turnaround between Tests is fine. Other teams are doing that as well.”Despite India’s poor Test run under his watch, with the team having lost 10 Tests since he took charge in July 2024, Gambhir said he remains unfazed.Asked about his discussions with selection chief Ajit Agarkar , Gambhir said, “It’s only about how we want to move forward in cricket. Rankings do not matter. We are not struggling. Since the England tour, we have played reasonable Test cricket.”
Article Summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has called for more three-Test series. He says they give teams an opportunity to recover after losing the opening match. India have lost 10 Tests since he took charge in July 2024, but he remains unfazed.

Kuldeep or Saransh?

Having found their ‘sweet spot’ in Tests, India will look to carry their winning momentum into the second and final game against an injury-hit Sri Lanka at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo on Sunday.Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant and left-arm spinner Manav Suthar were the stars of India’s 165-run win in Galle, with Suthar registering match figures of 10/131. If captain Shubman Gill and opener Yashasvi Jaiswal get going, India will fancy a 2-0 clean sweep in Colombo that would strengthen their push for a 2027 World Test Championship final slot and lift them from fifth to fourth in the standings.India’s last overseas Test series win came in the West Indies in July 2023, when they prevailed 1-0. Since then, they have lost 1-3 in Australia and drawn series in South Africa (1-1) and England (2-2). At home, they have suffered 0-3 and 0-2 whitewashes against New Zealand and South Africa respectively.The Galle victory, however, has revived their campaign. Padikkal (167 and 44), Rahul (82 and 35) and Pant (66) handled Sri Lanka’s spin attack adroitly, while Suthar underlined his credentials as a serious Test prospect.The focus will now turn to Gill and Jaiswal, both of whom struggled in Galle. Sri Lanka’s premier left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya dismissed Gill in both innings, while Jaiswal was run out in the first before edging Asitha Fernando to the wicketkeeper in the second.The key selection call is whether India persist with left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav , who took just one wicket for 103 runs in Galle, or hand a debut to 33-year-old off-spinning allrounder Saransh Jain. Jain could offer greater variety against Sri Lanka’s left-handers.

Article Title: From tape-ball cricket to 'dream of Harmanpreet’s wicket', Maryam Bibi follows her father’s unfulfilled dream
Article Text:
Hong Kong vice-captain Maryam Bibi

‘I had to work double hard in studies to play cricket’

Father’s unfinished dream became her motivation

'We got smashed' - but India A defeat became a lesson

'Harmanpreet is my dream wicket'

'It’s a huge responsibility' - Maryam on vice-captaincy

‘Sharing the pitch with India will inspire our girls’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hong Kong vice-captain Maryam Bibi is preparing for one of the biggest challenges of her career as her team gets ready to face India in the Women’s Asia Cup. For Maryam, the encounter is also a reminder of how far she and Hong Kong women’s cricket have come.Maryam's cricket journey began far away from the spotlight of international cricket. She started by playing tape-ball cricket with her father and continued playing the format during her primary-school years. It was only when she reached college and discovered hard-ball cricket that she decided to take the sport more seriously."I used to play tape-ball cricket with my dad and in primary school. When I went to college, we didn't have tape-ball cricket, we only had hard-ball cricket. For my enjoyment and loving cricket a lot, I wanted to try hard-ball cricket," Maryam told in an exclusive interview with Times of India.That decision eventually opened the door to a career with Hong Kong. After helping her school team win a championship, Maryam decided to test herself at the national level. She began attending national training sessions alongside club cricket before eventually earning her place in the Hong Kong setup.Her early journey also included selection for the 2018 ASEAN Cup tour to Thailand.For Maryam, pursuing cricket was never simply about turning up for training. Like many young athletes, she had to balance sport with education, but the demands were particularly challenging."In Hong Kong, studies are very important, and managing studies and cricket training was difficult for me, because my mom had a rule that I need to pass my studies to play cricket," she said."I have to train early morning and then train evening. So, I need to manage my studies and cricket. Which was one of the biggest obstacles for me," she added.Maryam credits her father as the biggest influence on her cricket career.Her father had dreamed of representing the national team but was unable to fulfil that ambition because of personal circumstances. Maryam eventually decided to carry that dream forward herself."My dad has the biggest influence on me, because my dad's dream was to play for a national side, and he couldn't play due to some personal reasons, So, I wanted to lift up his dream, and by doing that, I started dreaming to play for Hong Kong team," she said.Maryam has already experienced facing an Indian side, although it was India A, rather than the senior national team. Hong Kong played India A in the 2023 ACC Women's Emerging Teams Asia Cup. India A bowled Hong Kong out for just 34 before chasing the target in 5.2 overs to win by nine wickets. Shreyanka Patil took five wickets for two runs.Maryam remembers the experience vividly."I remember India A coming to Hong Kong and playing Emerging Cup, and we got smashed, for sure. We scored like 36 runs or something, and they chased it down in four overs," she said.But rather than allowing that defeat to define the team, Maryam believes it became an important learning experience."From that game, we had a lot of learnings and lessons we brought back, and in those two years' time, we focused on our fitness, skills and some of the analyst part of the game," she said.Now, Hong Kong are preparing to face India's senior side, and Maryam believes the approach has to be simple despite the huge difference in experience."We know that they are world-class batters and experienced players over there. Our thinking is to play the ball and take them... don't take them lightly, but don't play just because they're an India team. Play it as a game of cricket," she said.There is one Indian wicket Maryam would love to have on her resume. Asked which Indian batter she would most like to dismiss, Maryam immediately picked Harmanpreet Kaur "Harmanpreet Kaur, because I think she's my favourite, and she's my dream wicket. She's also a big player, a match-winner player, so I would love to dismiss her," she said.Maryam's cricketing influences extend beyond India. She named Harmanpreet Kaur and Ellyse Perry as two players she admires for completely different reasons."I love the aggression she has, like, the passion for cricket," Maryam said of Harmanpreet.On Perry, she added: "She's the calmest player I watched... her batting, the way she bats and bowls, and taking every situation very calmly. I just love the way she trains and carries herself on and out of the field."Maryam now occupies a leadership position within Hong Kong's women's team, serving as vice-captain. She sees the role not as a burden but as an opportunity to influence the next generation."I think it's a huge responsibility, and I think it's a privilege to have this responsibility. I never felt it's a burden," she said."As a player, I need to lead by example. I need to inspire young girls by setting an example for them, like how I train, how I am on and off the field, and how I can carry myself," she added.Her ambition extends beyond results. She wants to help create a stronger cricketing culture in Hong Kong."I want Hong Kong cricket to be better, not just by result, but also the belief and the culture way," she said.Maryam believes playing against India can have an impact that goes far beyond the result. For Hong Kong's young players, sharing the stage with established international stars offers an opportunity to learn directly from the best and gain exposure to a much bigger audience."Sharing the pitch... and also getting to know them, and if we get a chance to talk, and sharing the experience what they have, and learning from them will really inspire most of the girls who are here," she said."It will also give our Hong Kong girls broadcast visibility and everything, so I feel like it will be a good growth for them," Maryam added.While Maryam insists Hong Kong will give their best against all their opponents, she acknowledged that the clash against fellow associate side Thailand is a particularly important target."We should be doing our best in the three teams, but let's be honest about it, we are trying to put our best into the Thailand game," she said."My personal target will be to contribute in three departments, whether it's batting, bowling or fielding. I want to contribute... for a win. Any way possible, I'll contribute in all departments," she said.Although bowling remains her favourite discipline, she has been spending more time with the bat in recent months."Honestly speaking, I love bowling, but the past few months I've been batting a lot, so I'm looking forward to bat more," she said.For Maryam Bibi, therefore, the Women's Asia Cup is about more than simply facing one of the world's strongest teams. It is another chapter in a journey that began with tape-ball cricket alongside her father and has taken her to the Hong Kong national side and into a leadership role.Watch ACC Women's Asia Cup 2026 starting August 28, 2026, from 8 PM on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD and Sony LIV.
Article Summary: Hong Kong vice-captain Maryam Bibi is preparing for one of the biggest challenges of her career as her team gets ready to face India in the Women’s Asia Cup. Maryam's cricket journey began far away from the spotlight of international cricket. Her father had dreamed of representing the national team but was unable to fulfil that ambition.

Nabi earned his maiden call-up for the Lanka tour after scalping 104 wickets in the last two red-ball seasons for Jammu and Kashmir.Domestic players can draw inspiration from such journeys as they head into the Duleep Trophy, the curtain-raiser for the domestic season, at the BCCI Centre of Excellence on the outskirts of the city, beginning Sunday. The timing is significant, with the Indian team, which won four and lost five Tests last year, in a transitional phase. Ravindra Jadeja, 37, is in the twilight of his career, while KL Rahul, Axar Patel, Mohammed Siraj and Jasprit Bumrah are above 32.The door, therefore, could gradually open for a new crop to stake its claim for the near future.While talking about the future of Indian cricket, it is impossible to start a conversation without 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The Bihar boy has already made his T20 debut after a stunning IPL 2026 season. But there have been questions about whether the big-hitting 15-year-old has the patience and composure to play in the longer format. His 207 runs in eight first-class matches do not justify his skillset. At this juncture, the upcoming domestic seasons in red-ball cricket assume greater significance.Karnataka's R Smaran,23, the highest-run scorer in the Ranji Trophy last season with 950 runs, has also put his hat in the ring. The southpaw, who will turn up for South Zone, also scored 517 runs in the 24-25 season. Alongside Smaran, Vidarbha's left-arm spinner Harsh Dubey -- 83 wickets in his last two Ranji seasons-- and other contenders need to come up with solid seasons to even come up for discussions in the selectors' meeting for future Test series.After the Lanka Tests, India have two tricky New Zealand Tests (away, Nov), followed by tough five matches against Australia (home, Jan-Feb).Youngsters like Andhra batter SK Rasheed, 21, who have already played for India A, are making their presence felt. In the last two Ranji seasons, he has amassed 627 runs each. Against that backdrop, the Duleep Trophy, which begins with two quarterfinals (East Zone vs Northeast Zone; North Zone vs West Zone), will be an ideal stage for players to get some red-ball game time before the Ranji Trophy takes flight this Oct.For experienced players like Mohammed Shami, 35, Karun Nair, 34, and others eyeing a comeback, only top displays can remind the selectors of their hunger.Quarterfinals line up: East Zone vs NorthEast; North vs West.
Article Summary: Domestic circuit gives players a platform to make a case for promotion. Saransh Jain, Manav Suthar, Auqib Nabi and Sarfaraz Khan are proof that selectors delay but don’t deny consistent domestic performers. Duleep Trophy, the curtain-raiser for the domestic season, begins Sunday.

Article Title: After Joe Root, Ben Stokes calls ECB decision 'shambolic' over Headingley’s 2027 Ashes exclusion
Article Text:
Former captain Ben Stokes (image: IANS)

Headingley, Old Trafford left out of 2027 Ashes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Headingley holds special place in Ashes history

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes has hit out at the England and Wales Cricket Board's decision to leave Headingley out of the 2027 men's Ashes schedule, calling the move "shambolic". Stokes' comments came shortly after England's emphatic innings-and-103-run victory over Pakistan at Headingley in the first Test of their three-match series.Newly appointed Test captain Joe Root had earlier described Headingley's absence from next year's Ashes schedule as a "shame", pointing to England's outstanding record at the Leeds venue. Reacting to a social media post carrying Root's comments, Stokes said the word did not adequately describe his frustration."Shame is an understatement. Shambolic would be more appropriate. Great win though," Stokes wrote on his Instagram story.The ECB has selected Trent Bridge, Lord's, Edgbaston, the Rose Bowl (Utilita Bowl) and The Oval as the five venues for the 2027 men's Ashes series. The decision means there will be no Ashes Test in the north of England, with Headingley and Manchester's Old Trafford both missing from the schedule.The omission has attracted criticism given the history and significance of both venues in the Ashes. Headingley, in particular, has been one of England's most successful Test grounds in recent years and currently boasts a seven-match winning streak.The Leeds venue also has a special connection with Stokes. It was at Headingley during the 2019 Ashes that he produced one of the most memorable innings in Test history, scoring an unbeaten 135 to guide England to a dramatic one-wicket victory over Australia. Stokes' latest criticism comes after Root highlighted the significance of playing Ashes cricket in northern venues."It's a shame," Root had said following England's victory over Pakistan, referring to Headingley's omission from the 2027 schedule.While Headingley and Old Trafford are scheduled to return to the Ashes rotation in 2031, their absence from the 2027 series means northern England will go without a men's Ashes Test for the entire cycle between the two editions.
Article Summary: Ben Stokes hits out at decision to leave Headingley out of 2027 men's Ashes schedule. Article Title: Kuldeep Yadav or Saransh Jain? The subplot thickens as Colombo braces for a different script
Article Text:

TimesofIndia.com in Colombo:

Will he, won't he? Questions surrounding Kuldeep Yadav reached a fever pitch when the chinaman stayed away from the second training session in a row. While the official word from the Indian camp was that he was being rested from the first session, KL Rahul, who was also absent on Friday, turned up for a hit on Saturday.Kuldeep staying confined to the hotel room further raised eyebrows, as this is highly unusual, especially for an away fixture and particularly when he has bowled only 25 overs in the Galle Test. For a bowler who hardly missed training even when benched for all the Tests in England last summer, his absence in Colombo turned attention to Saransh Jain The 33-year-old got a good workout on both days, and his routine on the eve of the match has only thickened the subplot. Moments after reaching the ground, he went straight to the pitch to visualise before moving to the practice surface. Giving him company was Team India's spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule , and the duo spent some time talking and doing spot bowling before it was Saransh's turn to put the pads on.The left-hander switched nets and faced different combinations of net bowlers and throwdown specialists, watched by both head coach Gautam Gambhir and men's senior selection committee chairman Ajit Agarkar. The moment his batting session ended, Gambhir had a long chat with Saransh and even gave him a pat on the chest before the off-spinner left for the dressing room.Not just the cues from India's final net session, but Sri Lanka's addition of left-handers also points more strongly towards Saransh.Home captain Dhananjaya de Silva confirmed that Kamil Mishara, a left-hander, will take the opener's slot, and there is also the option of Sahan Arachchige, another southpaw, for the middle order.Gambhir kept his playing XI cards close to his chest at the pre-match press conference but asserted that the focus will be on assembling a bowling attack which gives them 20 wickets. Whether it will feature Saransh or Kuldeep wasn't revealed, but "all options" are open."We will try and pick the best bowling attack which will get us 20 wickets. You can score 1000 runs in Test cricket, there is no guarantee you are going to win a Test match but if you get 20 wickets, you have all the probability and possibility of winning the Test match. We will try and take the best attack that can get you 20 wickets, whether you have got three left-arm spinners in it or an offie or three seamers - we will have all our options open," said Gambhir.In the Galle Test, Kuldeep wasn't captain Shubman Gill's preferred option as he played the role of a third spinner in an attack also featuring Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja. The two finger spinners did the bulk of the bowling, and Gambhir reiterated that it was all about "getting the result"."Ultimately, we know how good a bowler Kuldeep is. And more importantly, sometimes, it's up to the captain as well, where he feels that if his two other spinners can get him wickets, looking at the conditions, what pace he wants a certain spinner to bowl. And it's not about guys underbowling and it's about getting the result. For me, I think that is more important," explained Gambhir."When you play five proper bowlers, someone will eventually get under-bowled. And that is what Test cricket is all about. It's not about someone not delivering and getting under-bowled. It's about who the captain feels or the management feel can be the most threatening in that particular condition," he added.Kuldeep was far from threatening across the two innings in Galle, returning with only one wicket. Bahutule revealed that Kuldeep was adapting and making changes based on the role assigned to him. Both Gambhir and Bahutule backed the chinaman, and the head coach revealed a very interesting conversation he had with the 31-year-old after the fixture."I think the conversation I have had with Kuldeep is just bowl your good spell rather than looking desperate to take wickets. Because sometimes, as a wrist spinner, when you are looking and you are desperate to take wickets, I think your control can go away as well. We rate Kuldeep very highly and we know how successful and how threatening he can be in every condition given to him. But again, I think the same thing, as I said, that we're going to try and pick the best type of what can deliver in these conditions," said Gambhir.There were no direct revelations, but plenty of undertones and cues have only increased the intrigue around Kuldeep vs Saransh.
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav stayed away from India's second training session in a row. Head coach Gautam Gambhir said it was all about "getting the result" Sri Lanka's addition of left-handers also points more strongly towards Saransh.

Article Title: 'Test cricket is dying': Chaminda Vaas urges boards to protect format
Article Text:
Sri Lanka's Keshara Nuwantha appeals during the first Test vs India in Galle (AFP Photo)

Sri Lanka's Test struggles

'We don't get a lot of Test matches'

Players must know their format

NEW DELHI: Test cricket is losing its place in a sport increasingly dominated by T20 leagues, and former Sri Lanka fast bowler Chaminda Vaas believes cricket boards must act before it is too late. Vaas, who played 111 Tests and claimed 355 wickets in his career, accepts that T20 cricket is likely to be the biggest format in the future. But he wants administrators to protect Test and one-day cricket, which he believes remain important for developing players and testing their skills.“I think in the future, most of the countries want to play T20s. T20 is the game for the future. But all the boards should realise that Test cricket and one-day cricket are the pioneers and they should preserve those two formats,” Vaas told PTI.The former Sri Lanka pacer made the comments amid a growing debate over the future of bilateral cricket and the increasing importance of franchise-based T20 leagues.Vaas, who took 400 wickets in ODIs and 355 in Tests, said cricket boards need to work together to protect the traditional formats.“We need to have some sort of arrangement to keep the 50-over cricket alive. I'm sure it will get a lot of young cricketers to play either Test cricket or 50-over format. But especially when it comes to Test cricket, Test cricket is dying. All the boards should have a plan to keep Test cricket alive and give a lot of youngsters the exposure to that format because it is where your skill will be really tested,” he said.Vaas pointed to Sri Lanka's recent decline in Test cricket as an example of what can happen when a team does not play enough red-ball cricket.Sri Lanka suffered a 165-run defeat against India in the first Test at Galle, a venue that was once considered one of the team's strongest home grounds.Vaas, however, praised India for their performance.“We know India is a very good side, they can replace any player at any given point. They have been playing good cricket across Test, T20 and ODIs, and the BCCI has built some excellent infrastructure and taken care of their players.“If you look at Galle, they played excellent Test cricket. They fielded three very good spinners and it was not easy to survive against them. Our guys gave a good fight. I'm sure that the second Test will be a more interesting one,” he said.But he believes the defeat is also linked to a bigger problem - Sri Lanka simply does not play enough Tests.Vaas said Sri Lanka needs to play more red-ball cricket if it wants to produce players who can succeed at Test level.“Unfortunately, we don't get a lot of Test matches. The Sri Lankan cricket board should do something, try to get more Tests. You know, this two-match Test series does not really benefit the players, they need more red-ball matches at the highest level,” he said.He believes playing only a small number of Tests makes it harder for young players to develop the skills required at the highest level.The former pacer also said players need to understand which format suits their game.“There are players who can play all versions — Test cricket, one-day and T20. But some other players can only play white ball. So, we need to identify those players and even the players should realise which format they are going to play and be comfortable with. But for me, Test cricket is the real skill. You need to have that skill to play in the middle. So whatever the format they choose, they do the right thing and should focus on the basics,” he said.
Article Summary: Chaminda Vaas says Test cricket is losing its place in a sport dominated by T20 leagues. Former Sri Lanka fast bowler believes cricket boards must act before it is too late. Vaas accepts that T20 cricket is likely to be the biggest format in the future.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest.
